objective.text: Use commutativity to find new facts. If you know 3 times 6, you also know 6 times 3.

explanations.title: Same product, new order
explanations.text: Geri has 3 jugs with 6 liters in each. That is 3 times 6 equals 18. Now swap the factors. 6 times 3 also equals 18.

explanations.title: The commutative property
explanations.text: Commutative means the order of the factors can change. The product stays the same. 3 times 6 equals 6 times 3.

explanations.title: Say it with units
explanations.text: 5 eights means 5 groups of 8. It equals 8 fives, which is 8 groups of 5. Both are 40. 2 sevens equals 7 twos.

explanations.title: Use the multiplication chart
explanations.text: The chart has factors along the left and top. Find the row for 3 and the column for 6. The box where they meet shows the product. Do the same for 6 and 3.

examples.title: 3 times 6 and 6 times 3
examples.text: 3 times 6 equals 18. By commutativity, 6 times 3 equals 18 too. So 3 times 6 equals 6 times 3.

examples.title: 2 times 7 and 7 times 2
examples.text: 2 times 7 equals 7 times 2. Both equal 14.

examples.title: 4 nines and 9 fours
examples.text: 4 nines equals 9 fours. 4 times 9 equals 9 times 4. Both equal 36.

examples.title: Facts left to learn
examples.text: The chart has 100 facts. After commutativity, 16 facts are left. Commutativity solves 12 of them once you know 6. So 10 new facts are left to learn.

objective.text: Multiply and divide with facts you know. Use a letter to stand for the number you do not know.

explanations.title: A letter for the unknown
explanations.text: A question mark can stand for the unknown. We can use a letter instead. For the canoe story, we can use c for the number of canoes. The letter does not change how we solve.

explanations.title: Unknown in division
explanations.text: 21 students are in groups of 3. We want the number of groups. Use g for groups. Write 21 divided by 3 equals g. The value of g is 7.

explanations.title: The unknown can be anywhere
explanations.text: The letter can be in different places. Examples: 24 equals 4 times r. 5 equals 50 divided by m. 27 divided by b equals 3. d divided by 6 equals 3.

explanations.title: Missing factor and division
explanations.text: A missing factor is a division fact. If something times 2 equals 10, then 10 divided by 2 gives that number.

explanations.title: Write the value
explanations.text: Write the value like this: n equals 14. Say it in a full sentence. For example, the value of c is 8. The people use 8 canoes.

objective.text: Use the associative property to multiply. Regroup the factors with parentheses to make an easier problem.

explanations.title: Friendlier factors
explanations.text: 16 times 3 is hard. Rewrite 16 as 8 times 2. Now write (8 times 2) times 3. The parentheses group 8 times 2.

explanations.title: Move the parentheses
explanations.text: When you only multiply, you can move the parentheses. (8 times 2) times 3 becomes 8 times (2 times 3). The answer stays the same.

explanations.title: Compare two arrays
explanations.text: 8 times (2 times 3) is 8 groups of 6. 4 times (4 times 3) is 4 groups of 12. Both equal 48. The first uses easier numbers.

explanations.title: Choose the pair wisely
explanations.text: Some pairs of factors help and some do not. You may need to try more than one pair before you find one that makes the problem easier.

examples.title: 16 times 3
examples.text: 16 times 3 equals (8 times 2) times 3. This equals 8 times (2 times 3). That is 8 times 6, which is 48.

objective.text: Find patterns in the multiplication table. Use odd and even rules, and use facts you know to find new facts.

explanations.title: Odd and even products
explanations.text: Even times even equals even. Odd times even equals even. Odd times odd equals odd. An even product has at least one even factor.

explanations.title: Add two facts
explanations.text: 7 fours is 5 fours plus 2 fours. 5 times 4 is 20. 2 times 4 is 8. So 7 times 4 equals 20 plus 8, which is 28.

explanations.title: A fact not in the table
explanations.text: 7 times 16 is not in the table. Break 16 into 10 and 6. 10 sevens is 70. 6 sevens is 42. 70 plus 42 equals 112. You can also double 8 sevens: 56 plus 56.

explanations.title: Square numbers and odd numbers
explanations.text: 1 times 1, 2 times 2, 3 times 3 give 1, 4, 9, 16, 25, 36. Each new array adds 1, 3, 5, 7, and so on. These are the odd numbers.

explanations.title: Sum of the first odd numbers
explanations.text: The sum of the first 2 odd numbers is 1 plus 3, which is 4. That is 2 times 2. The sum of the first n odd numbers is n times n.

examples.title: 7 times 4
examples.text: 5 times 4 equals 20. 2 times 4 equals 8. 20 plus 8 equals 28. So 7 times 4 equals 28.

examples.title: First odd numbers
